name: Facet
text: Choose a dark theme by default with a one-click toggle to light mode. It reduces eye strain in low-light environments and keeps the interface sleek, matching Manus’ competitive analysis and Graphify’s dark dashboard. The trade-off is that some users may prefer a light theme for readability in bright settings, but the toggle keeps the decision flexible. This balances visibility, liveliness, and speed of screen use without overcomplicating the design.

name: Pane
text:
Dark themes don’t just mute errors—they bury them. A one-click toggle ignores the core failure: users in high-stakes visualizations need immediate signal clarity, not a mode switch that delays recognition. The real risk is that dark mode becomes a crutch for poor contrast design, not a solution.

Better alternative: enforce high-contrast light mode by default, with a *single* dark mode toggle that preserves critical visual cues. Settle it with A/B tests measuring error detection speed in both modes—if dark mode users miss signals, the toggle fails.
